title: Reconstructing non-Abelian braiding and fusion without anyon transport
authors: Lucy Byles, Matthew D. Horner, Benjamin T. H. Varcoe, Jiannis K. Pachos
abstract: Non-Abelian anyons offer a route to fault-tolerant and universal quantum computing, but experimental access to their defining braiding and fusion data remains limited by the resource overhead of implementing extended anyonic processes on quantum hardware. Here we introduce and experimentally realise a measurement-only protocol based on temporally ordered ribbon operations that reconstructs the non-Abelian braiding and fusion primitives of the quantum double model $D(S_3)$ without physical anyon transport. We implement a reduced two-qutrit version of the protocol on Quantinuum's H2 trapped-ion processors, realising ancilla-assisted ribbon operations and anyonic charge projections in a qubit encoding. We reconstruct the squared braiding phases and fusion amplitudes using an adapted Hadamard test and post-selected measurements, respectively. The associated braiding and fusion transformations reproduce their ideal actions with average normalised output-state fidelities of $\overline{\mathcal{F}}_{R}=0.9988$ and $\overline{\mathcal{F}}_{F}=0.9987$. Combining these primitives produces a non-Clifford braid and a non-stabilizer resource state, supporting measurement-only anyonic encodings as building blocks for larger topologically encoded quantum processors.
summary: The authors developed and experimentally demonstrated a novel, resource-efficient method to measure non-Abelian braiding and fusion properties for topological quantum computing using only local measurements on trapped ions. By implementing this on Quantinuum's H2 system, they achieved high fidelities, proving that complex anyonic operations can be simulated without physically moving the anyons.
main_problem: The research aims to reconstruct the defining non-Abelian braiding and fusion data for topological quantum computation without needing physical transport of anyons.
main_result: They successfully reconstructed these primitives with high fidelities ($\overline{\mathcal{F}}_{R}=0.9988$ and $\overline{\mathcal{F}}_{F}=0.9987$), demonstrating measurement-only protocols for building larger topological quantum processors.
method: The protocol uses a measurement-only approach based on temporally ordered ribbon operations, adapted Hadamard tests for braiding phases, and post-selected measurements for fusion amplitudes.
model_or_system: The study models the system using the quantum double model $D(S_3)$ and implements the reduced two-qutrit version of the protocol on Quantinuum's H2 trapped-ion processors.

main_assumptions: The reconstruction relies on reducing higher-dimensional overlaps to effective two-qutrit operations and using specific input states for the Hadamard test.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the plaquette diagram of the reduced protocol, the spacetime sequence for braiding measurement (Fig. 1b), hardware circuits for testing phases via adapted Hadamard tests (Fig. 2), and circuit diagrams for fusion amplitude reconstruction (Fig. 3a).
paper_structure: The paper details the theoretical framework for non-Abelian anyons, presents the measurement-only protocol using ribbon operations on trapped ions, describes the specific circuits for measuring braiding phases via Hadamard tests, and concludes with high-fidelity results confirming the feasibility of these building blocks.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses a major bottleneck in topological quantum computation—the difficulty of accessing fundamental anyonic data—by proposing an entirely measurement-based protocol applicable to trapped-ion hardware.
